text:
Ellen: heads up from oncall: during the cross-region failover yesterday a handful of sessions ended up using a higher-cost model because regional policy bundles had slightly different penalty deltas. Not a big outage but cost spike for a few tenants. Thinking about long-term fixes.

Finn: seen this too. root cause: two control-plane writers applied overlapping rule changes; order differed by region so penalty arithmetic ended up asymmetric. Runtime just applies whatever compiled bundle it has.

Gita: idea: make policy bundles contain an immutable `apply_id` (UUID) plus a deterministic merge function for deltas so that order doesn't matter. merge function example: per-rule last-writer-wins by `apply_id` timestamp + tie-breaker by writer-id.

Harpreet: LWW works but loses intent when deltas are commutative only under combination semantics. e.g., a delta that "increase penalty by 5" vs one that "set penalty to 20" are different ops. We should treat deltas as typed ops: set vs add vs multiply, and provide a canonical normalization step that converts ops to a canonical form before merging.

Ellen: totally agree on typed ops. could we also attach a short-term session affinity token so existing sessions keep their route while reconciliation finishes? something like `x-policy-grace: ttl=90s, mode=sticky`. That avoids mid-request switch and extra hedges.

Finn: sticky header + canonical merge seems pragmatic. Implementation plan: (1) normalize deltas to canonical ops in policy-svc (2) publish compiled bundle with `apply_id` and `bundle_hash` (sha256) (3) runtimes add `x-policy-apply` header to decisions and honor `sticky` for active sessions.

Gita: observability: emit traces with `bundle_hash` and metric `bundle_mismatch_count`. ops wants an alert when mismatch_count > 10 in any 5m window. Also we should surface last-3 apply_ids in the console for debugging.

ops-bot: ops-bot: alert configured: bundle_mismatch_count > 10 in 5m -> paging: oncall-eng.

Harpreet: note on rollbacks: we need a forced-rollback endpoint that can atomically mark a given apply_id as "revoked" and signal runtimes to stop honoring sticky tokens (so they can converge back). That RPC must be rate-limited and require SSO + 2FA.

Ellen: action items: Finn + Gita iterate on canonical op set + normalization POC. Harpreet to draft operator rollback endpoint security requirements. I'll write up a short RFC for sticky-session semantics and console UI bits.

Finn: I'll prototype bundle_hash computation and a lightweight sticky token flow for the runtime (opt-in flag). Microbench on overhead next week.

Gita: I'll add telemetry hooks for bundle history and the mismatch metric.

Ellen: timeline: RFC this week, POC next sprint, canary in a single region after tests. thanks all. :raised_hands:
